$comment: ★★ EVERY INTEGER WIDTH TO `float`, BIT FOR BIT (P68 round 12, D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN). Each value is converted by a plain C cast from a `volatile` and the float's BIT PATTERN is compared with the correctly rounded value computed in exact rational arithmetic by the lane's conversion-matrix generator (round to nearest, ties to even, ONE rounding) — signed and unsigned 8, 16, 32 and 64-bit sources at their extremes and at the values that sit just past a rounding boundary. Checks 24, 25, 30 and 31 are the values a conversion through `double` rounds TWICE and lands on a different float (e.g. 2^63 + 2^39 + 1: 0x5F000001 correctly, 0x5F000000 through binary64), so a realization that detours through F64 fails them. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-24 before the change: DSS refused every int->float conversion with an F32 result on x86_64 PE, x86_64 ELF and arm64 ELF, debug and release (`L_UnsupportedLoweringForOpcode … only an F64 (double) destination`); gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (-O0/-O2), aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc under qemu, mingw-w64 gcc and MSVC 19.51 (/Od, /O2) run the same conversions to 42. The `release` arm pins the same file through the shipped release pipeline.
